cohorts.subjects: Living symptomatic adults (low back pain with or without radiculopathy) referred for lumbar MRI to the Department of Radiology, Chalmeda Anand Rao Institute of Medical Sciences, Karimnagar, Telangana, India, June 2017 to October 2018; all consented; Telangana state population, ethnicity not otherwise stated. Excluded: age under 20, previous lumbar spine surgery, vertebral trauma, tumours, infections, congenital anomalies (number excluded not stated). Cross-sectional study.
cohorts.n_units: 80 people, L1 to L5 each (two diameters per level)

techniques.instrument: GE Signa HDxt 1.5 T, sense spine coil, 4 mm slice thickness; sequences T2W FSE sagittal, T1W FSE sagittal, STIR coronal, T1W and T2W FSE axial, high-resolution T2 FSE drive axial with small FOV; images read in INSTARAD viewer version 1.7, values in mm. Figure 1's overlay: Sag T2, TR 2780 ms, TE 119.2 ms, ST 4.3 mm, ETL 25, 512 x 512, readout to 0.01 cm
techniques.how: On the T2-weighted mid-sagittal image, from the midpoint of the vertebral body's posterior border (where the basivertebral vein leaves the body) to the most anterior point of the spinous process, at each of L1 to L5. How the level was numbered and how the mid-sagittal slice was chosen are not stated.

within_paper: The two diameters (Tables 1 and 2) are measured on the same 80 patients (p. 22, PDF 2). The Present study columns of Table 3 and Table No.4 repeat Tables 1 and 2 for the same subjects (p. 25, PDF 5). Figures 1 and 2 show one female patient aged 40 by the overlay, the same person in both figures (p. 23, PDF 3; Inference: same overlay identifier and study date); Inference: she is one of the 80, which the paper does not state. Alam et al [13] in Table 3 and M Alam et al. [13] in Table No.4 cite one reference (p. 25, PDF 5), so they are one cohort, alam_ct, measured two ways; Amonoo-Kuofi [6] (radiographs) and [7] (cadaveric) are two papers whose subject overlap is not stated.
